summary: A small test server that starts the schedule app on a free local port and prints that port number so a browser test can connect.
purpose: Gives the browser test for the assembly view a separate, isolated backend that does not touch real jobs.
why: Using a fresh random port avoids clashes with other servers, and printing the port lets the test find it.
how: When run directly, it opens a socket on the local machine with port zero, which asks the system for any free port. It prints that port number on its own line and flushes output immediately so the test can read it. It then starts the uvicorn web server on that existing socket with error-only logging, using the app returned by create_app.
inputs: No command-line input is read. It uses the app factory from the schedule3d package.
outputs: A line printed to standard output in the form of the port label followed by the number, then a running web server on that port.
risks: If the reader of the output reads the wrong line or waits too long, the browser test may fail to connect. The socket is not closed explicitly before the server takes it over, which is intended here. Error-only logging hides routine request details, which makes failures harder to diagnose.
debug: If the browser test cannot find the port, run this file directly and check the printed line. If the server does not start, check that uvicorn and the schedule3d package are installed. If requests fail, check the app factory for startup errors.
